newsitem.title: USA: U.S. money managers go longer on U.S. debt -- MCM.
newsitem.headline: U.S. money managers go longer on U.S. debt -- MCM.

text.p: U.S. fixed-income managers took advantage of others' year-end selling to take longer positions in U.S. debt markets over the past week, according to an MCM MoneyWatch Inc survey.

"These investors have been using weakness to add duration, not seeing anything wrong with the fundamental landscape," said MCM money market analyst Peter McTeague, who conducts the asset allocation survey.
The weekly survey showed durations as a percentage of benchmark rose to 108.3 percent in the week ended December 23 from 108.1 percent in the prior week.
A duration reading above 100 percent indicates the group of investors polled is mostly long on the market.
A portfolio's duration represents its average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
In the "next likely move" category, portfolio managers representing 25 percent of total assets in the survey said they would "buy," up from 22 percent the prior week.
Strategists leaning toward "sell" rose to 22 percent, up from 21 percent in the week ended December 16.
Fifty-three percent of managers said they were "neutral" on the market, down from 57 percent a week ago.
Cash as a percentage of assets rose to 2.36 percent, against 2.16 percent registered the previous week.

The survey showed 31 percent of investors polled overweighted the 10-plus years duration sector, up from 29 percent the previous week, while 10 percent underweighted it. The remaining 59 percent were "neutral."
In the five- to 10-year duration sector, 44 percent of investors polled said they overweighted the securities and 12 percent underweighted them.
The survey included 38 domestic participants, who manage about $100 billion in fixed-income assets. The poll is conducted weekly by MCM and usually is released on Tuesday.
